spec.notes: Written to C:\Users\Rahma\CryoLean\research\v4\scene\lake_shore_ccs_cp_200mm_wired.json. Sources: Lake Shore CCS-CP datasheet (ccr-large-sample-space.pdf, cached research/v5/cache/4d5c7f00e97af8bd.txt) and product page (cached 0e493d121b7537b0.txt). Only two stage temperatures are documented: cold plate <4 K (408/415/418 options) and 300 K max; the first-stage temperature_K=300 is a schema placeholder, not a measurement. The cryogen enum 'cryogen_free_gm' is a forced choice: the datasheet says only 'closed-cycle refrigerator' with 'cold head' options 408/415/418 and never names GM or pulse tube; treat the cold-head motion type as unverified. outer.height/width values are labelled as compressor height and cold-plate diameter respectively because the cryostat shroud dimensions are unpublished; renderers should not treat them as shroud dimensions. Temperature stability ±50 mK measured with the included Model 346 controller (100 W heater output). Water-cooled compressor needs 6-9 L/min at 5-25 °C; air-cooled alternative is 450 x 485 x 925 mm, 155 kg. Recommended maintenance 13,000 h (cryostat), 30,000 h compressor, 10,000 h cold head. A web search found no published CCS-CP outline drawing.

spec.notes: Vertical cryogen-free PPMS: a single Cryomech two-stage pulse tube sits in helium gas in a 'bucket' tank (not vacuum-mounted); first stage ~45 K cools the main and annulus radiation shields and cryopump stage 1; the second stage condenses He onto a ~150 cc LHe pool that cools the 4 K Plate by thermosiphon; the switch-less 14 T NbTi solenoid is conduction-cooled by solid contact to the 4 K Plate and produces a vertical (longitudinal) field at 120 A full field. The sample chamber (2.5 cm clear bore) runs down the magnet bore; 4.2 K helium from the bucket passes a counter-flow heat exchanger and mass-flow controller (0-5000 sccm) into the cooling annulus around the chamber and returns via the circulation scroll pump (5-50 Torr return, 500-800 Torr outlet), giving 1.8-400 K at the puck. The puck (2.3 cm Cu, Au plated) plugs into the 12-pin keyed connector at the chamber bottom; the block thermometer is clamped to the puck interface outside the chamber. Magnet centre 4.05 cm above puck surface; 14 T uniformity +/-0.1% over 5.5 cm on axis. Options modelled: ETO (2 channels), VSM (linear transport motor on the top KF flange, 6.3 mm coil bore, 9 mm coil separation, 40 Hz x 2 mm) and Heat Capacity (3 x 3 mm platform, puck microcalorimeter in high vacuum via the integrated cryopump). No optical windows in this configuration (magneto-optic FOSH option not installed). Outer dimensions are D x W x H for cryostat plus can rack; the 67x70x100 cm electronics cabinet and 69x50x62 cm compressor stand apart. 14 T startup 40 h typical; puck 300 K to 1.9 K in under 40 min. spec.notes: Written to C:\Users\Rahma\CryoLean\research\v4\scene\qdoxford_optistatdn_v_ln2.json. Compact tabletop LN2 bath optical cryostat, 175 x 175 x 450 mm, 5 kg (manual Table 3-5 and 7.3). Top: LN2 fill/vent pipe, nitrogen exhaust flow needle valve, two 10-pin connectors (diagnostic, experimental) on the OVC top plate, DN16NW OVC evacuation port with pressure-relief plates. Inside: 1.2 L LN2 reservoir around a central heat-exchanger support tube; capillary feeds a gravity-fed heat exchanger carrying heater + PT100; sample holder (20 x 50 mm) bolts beneath, sample in vacuum ('No cold windows'). Four radial Spectrosil WF windows + one axial blank, each held by four nylon screws and an O-ring, 35 mm clear aperture, f/1 (QD Oxford page: 'Large illumination area: 35 mm diameter window aperture'; 'Weight: 5 kg'). Charcoal sorb with 150 ohm heater keeps the OVC below 1e-4 mbar. 77.2-500 K, +/-0.1 K, cooldown 20 min, hold >= 15 h. No cryocooler, no magnet; only motion is LN2 boil-off vapour at the vent and the optional external pump. Sources: QD Oxford Optistat matrix PDF (cache c73e273061693731), QD Oxford product page (cache 295cbbaf14723ca3), Oxford Instruments Optistat family brochure (cache d52046bdb551703d, newly snapshotted), Oxford Instruments Optistat DN-V Operators Manual Issue 2.0 Dec 2020 (andor.oxinst.com robots.txt disallows the snapshot script; PDF fetched via WebFetch and text extracted locally with pypdf into the session scratchpad, not research/v5/cache). spec.notes: Cryostat-100 is a vertical cylindrical LN2 boil-off calorimeter, not a sample cryostat: the 'stages' are the LN2-filled cold mass (78 K cold boundary) and the 293 K heater sleeve warm boundary; the 'sample' is an annular insulation shell wrapped around the cold mass. Published dimensions cover only the cold mass (167/168 mm diameter, 1 m / 1026 mm with guards; test-chamber effective length 575 mm per patent: 'using an effective length of the cold mass of 575 mm, the mean surface area for heat transfer through a typical 25-mm thick insulation test article is 0.35 m 2'). The vacuum canister's outer size is not published anywhere found, so the outer block carries cold-mass numbers with that stated; the canister must be modelled as a slightly larger stainless cylinder with a domed lid without quoting a dimension. Vacuum range: below 1x10-5 torr to 760 torr (NTRS 20150011030). Cold mass suspended by six Kevlar threads ('six KEVLAR threads with hooks and hardware for attachment and length adjustment', patent); CO2-filled vapor-pocket disks separate guard and test vessels; bake-out heaters on the canister exterior. spec.notes: Static pour-fill LN2 cryostat: no cryocooler, no pump inside the cryostat, no magnet; the only motion is LN2 boil-off vapour from the 400 mL top reservoir. Configured without VPF-PM pumping manifold so range is 77-500 K. Weight 3.3 kg (7 lb). The instrumentation adapter (brochure) carries a 10-pin electrical feedthrough, three spare o-ring sealed ports, an evacuation valve and a pressure relief valve; the wired variant WH-10P gives 10 PhBr twisted pairs. The stage temperature_K values are the 77 K base (both reservoir and mount sit at LN2 temperature when not heated). Window material default is fused silica (WR-STD-FS); sapphire, ZnSe, CaF2, KBr, TPX are 3 mm or 6 mm options. Single source: 800 Series Cryostream Operating and Instruction Guide, Oxford Cryosystems 2014 (SFU mirror), text cached at research/v5/cache/4dfb8bc9e86001d6.txt (65 pages). Cryostream Plus differs from the standard only by its 500 K upper limit (Section 5.1); all geometry is identical. Physical layout from the manual: coldhead with integral vacuum-insulated transfer line (1500 mm flexible + 905 mm rigid leg, min bend radius 200 mm, ~900 mm leg uses top 850 mm of dewar) plunged into the unpressurised 60 L ES60 dewar (NW50 KF neck, 50 mm bore); coldhead clamped in the Varibeam stand with fine X/Y/Z translation; red 6 mm PTFE dry-air tube to the coldhead; 3.5 m Coldhead Cable to the controller (placed < 3 m from coldhead, < 2 m from the gas pump). Vacuum space re-pumped every 12-18 months via the pump-out adaptor (NW16/KF16) with the CRH25 re-activation heater. Nothing moves in the coldhead itself: the only motion is the N2 gas flow driven by the separate gas pump, the dry-air shroud, and LN2 consumption/boil-off from the dewar. 'outer' uses the Varibeam stand envelope (600 mm height, 430 mm reach) because the coldhead body has no published dimensions. spec.notes: Written to C:\Users\Rahma\CryoLean\research\v4\scene\oxford_optistatdry_blv.json. Sources: OptistatDry BLV manual MAN-OPTDRY-BLV-2.1.0 Sep 2017 (andor.oxinst.com; robots.txt blocked scripts/v5_snapshot.py so it was fetched with WebFetch and text-extracted with pypdf into the scratchpad), OptistatDry brochure doc 4694 (2018) 'Cool down time from ambient to 4.2 K < 160 minutes at 50 Hz; Typical cooling power 0.2 W at 4.2 K; Optical access 28 mm diameter clear view, f1', Optistat matrix PDF (research/v5/cache/c73e273061693731.txt) and QD-Oxford product page (research/v5/cache/295cbbaf14723ca3.txt). Geometry: vertical cryostat body (OVC with SHI 101D two-stage GM cold head on top, He gas lines entering at the rear), narrowing to an 80 mm optical window block tail at the bottom with four radial window ports (f/1, 28 mm clear view) and one axial port underneath (blanked as standard); each OVC window held by an O-ring and 4 M3 nylon screws, with a matching radiation-shield window/blank held by a spring clip. Radiation shield is cooled by the GM first stage and carries the charcoal sorb on its removable front plate; sample platform/puck bolts to the heat exchanger on the GM second stage. Whole cryostat hangs in a stand with two side panels, cradle on four anti-vibration mounts (M6, 25 mm fine height adjust) and radial restraints in the OVC T-slots. Standard wiring here is the 12-track PCB puck (12P code); the alternative LX20 20-pin option (nine constantan twisted pairs + one copper pair) is not part of this configuration. Vibration <10 um RMS at the sample. Cooldown RT to base ~3.0 h (DC12 puck). Temperature control by Mercury iTC (450 W).

spec.notes: Scene: vertical aluminium OVC of stacked cylindrical sections on a cross-braced steel frame; inside, top plate -> PT1 (77 K) -> PT2 (4 K copper shield, magnet hangs from it) -> still (700 mK shield) -> cold plate (100 mK) -> 360 mm mixing chamber plate (< 10 mK; MX450 guaranteed > 450 uW at 100 mK, > 12 uW at 20 mK). One Sumitomo RP-182B2S pulse tube (PTR options 1.35/1.50/1.80 W; 1.5 W = RP-182B2S) with separated valve unit. One 117 x 252 mm Secondary Insert slot carries the BLL-72 bottom-loader SI with cold finger: 28 SMA hermetic + 4 x 24-way Fischer at room temperature, 28 SMP + 2 x 51-way Nano-D at the cold finger, plus one spare ISO100 LOS port (up to 37 coax). The 72 mm x 144 mm puck enters from below through a vacuum lock on a removable loading arm; load < 15 min, 10 h cooldown, < 12 mK and 150 uW at 100 mK at the puck. 14 T solenoid, quench protected, ramps to full field in 1 h or less; patented gas-gap heat switches with a remote sorb (outgassed at ~30 K) link the plates. Also 2 x KF40 + 2 x KF25 LOS ports on the top plate. CAVEATS: PT1/PT2/still/cold-plate temperatures and the 2 m x 0.6 m outer size come from the published Sheffield QSHS Proteox MX500 (8 T custom magnet), the closest documented Proteox MX, not an MX450 datasheet. The catalog unknown stands: the 14 T + 72 mm / 28-coax pairing is 'Dependent on magnet selection' and undocumented; the BLL-60 (77 mm bore, 22 coax, 96 DC) may be the actual 14 T puck. A Pisa MX450 (no magnet) is wired with 7 coax, 2 x 24-wire DC looms and 2 single-mode fibres (cisup.unipi.it/?p=5370), a different real-world wiring. spec.notes: Scene: a bare single-stage Gifford-McMahon cold head, not a cryostat. Geometry from Cryomech drawing CH1A600 rev A (supersedes CH10600): 241.3 mm room-temperature flange; 267.7 mm motor housing with two eyebolts above the flange; 127 mm diameter cold cylinder 307.8 mm long below the flange ending in a bare copper heat exchanger (8x M10 on 101.6 mm BC). Two 3/4 inch Aeroquip helium couplings exit the side 57.2 mm above the flange, reaching 237.8 mm from the axis. Cold head weight 42 kg. Separate water-cooled CPA1114 compressor 61 x 61 x 79 cm, 191 kg, 440/480 VAC 3-phase 60 Hz, 12.5 kW, joined by two 3 m (10 ft) 1 inch ID flex lines (6.8 kg per pair) and a motor cord of the same length. Performance: 600 W at 80 K certified at 60 Hz, 510 W at 70 K, 350 W at 50 K, <=25 K no load, <1 h cooldown. The spec sheet's '430 W at 600 K' is a typo for the 60 K point. Animation: displacer reciprocates inside the cold cylinder at an unpublished GM rate; compressor hum at mains frequency; helium pulses in the flex lines. Floor-standing painted box cabinet 985 W x 1193 D x 2054 H mm with ONE full-opening front door (family page says two doors except 'one door on 2.0 models'); stainless interior 685 x 685 x 736 mm (233 L). Thermal system: LN2 injected through vacuum-jacketed valves/manifold (proportional manifold is optional on 2.0, so standard is on/off solenoid valves), nichrome heaters in an overhead plenum, high-velocity recirculating air; -100 to 200 C, 70 C/min empty, 208/230 V 1ph 70 A. No vacuum, no magnet. Standard configuration has no window (cabinet option 'Windows and ports' not fitted) and no sample feedthrough ports; the only documented sample-side signal path is the PLC's four spare thermocouple input channels (product thermocouple is an instrumentation option). For the 3D model: single-zone box with a door on the front face, plenum at the top of the interior containing heaters and LN2 injection, air circulating downward over the workspace; an LN2 supply line (Dewar or bulk tank) enters from outside. The PLC/desktop PC with flat panel monitor is a separate item whose dimensions are not published.

spec.notes: Sources: Lake Shore FWPX technical-specifications page (cache research/v5/cache/9ae700052f15978d.txt) and Lake Shore Probe Stations catalog PDF probestationcatalog_l.pdf pp. 38-39 (cache research/v5/cache/75efd8eb8da79422.txt), whose cross-section diagram labels 'Radiation shield stage (20 K) / Sample stage (4.5 K) / Probe (25 K) / Probe arm base / Probe arm shield / Thermal anchors / Vacuum chamber base'. Scene geometry: a 406 mm OD x 178 mm tall nickel-plated aluminium vacuum chamber (330 mm top opening, 102 mm fused-quartz top viewport with 91 mm viewing area, NW40 pump port with isolation valve, NW25 gauge port, 0.25 in NPT gas port, 3.5 kPa relief valve) on a 1067 x 851 mm platform; inside, a nickel-plated aluminium radiation shield with 180 mm lid and 159 mm IR-absorbing window (152 mm viewing area) surrounds the 4.5 K x-y translating sample stage carrying a 102 mm grounded SH-4.00-G sample holder; six micromanipulated probe arms enter from the sides, arm anchored to the 20 K shield, probe anchored to the sample stage. Cooling is a 2-stage continuous-flow cryostat (sample + radiation shield) fed by a large-bore S-style LHe/LN2 transfer line with 12.7 mm top-port Dewar withdrawal; no compressor or cold head, so the only mechanical motion is cryogen flow, the pump, and operator-driven stage/probe moves. Base 4.5 K with up to 6 arms (3.5 K with PS-LT, not fitted); control range 5-475 K on the current web page (4.5-420 K in the catalog PDF); cooldown 1.5 h, warmup 1.5 h, cycle 3.5 h, vibration <30 nm, base pressure <1e-5 Torr, no magnet option, no backside optical access. The 'lhe_flow' enum covers both cryogens: the same flow circuit runs on LN2 (80 K) or LHe (5 K). Written to research/v4/scene/lakeshore_fwpx_6arm_standard.json.

spec.notes: ILL pool unit 82ILHV100: 'Type | Orange Ø100', 'Quad-exchanger', 1.5-320 K, Ø100 x 265 mm sample space, aluminium A5-AG3 in beam, top loading for high-pressure measurements. Wet cryostat: LN2 bath + LHe bath, cold valve + capillary to the heat exchanger, He vapour drawn through the annulus to a roots/rotary pump for <4.2 K (ISIS: 2 psi feed, 50 ohm 100 W max heater, cooldown 3.5-4 h for 100 mm, 10-15 min from 20 K to 1.5 K). ILL manual: sample chamber pumped with a primary pump then 20 cc helium exchange gas admitted via blue 3-way valve; isolation vacuum pumped <1e-5 with a turbo. AS Scientific has built the Orange under ILL licence since 1981 (ILL history page); 2015 exchanger modification 'operates three times faster'. Outer-dimension values above are from NIST's 100 mm Orange (same ILL design) and are a top-flange-to-beam distance and the well bore only; the renderer should treat vessel/tail diameters as unpublished. spec.notes: Scene: a floor-standing industrial Stirling cryogenerator box 1.0 m x 0.7 m x 1.65 m, 550 kg, not a cryostat. Datasheet SPC-1 (2026/01): single-stage reversed Stirling cycle, 400 W - 2.7 kW at 50-160 K, graph conditions 30 barg helium at 1455 rpm, water-cooled (1200 l/h, 20% glycol), 3-phase 400 V/50 Hz or 480 V/60 Hz, max process gas 20 barg, < 72 dBA, > 8000 h maintenance interval. Catalog capability 400 W at 77/80 K comes from the net N2/O2 cooling-power curve. Product page: process heat exchanger integrated in the cold head; PLC controlled; all rotating/reciprocating seals at ambient temperature; units exist in 1- or 4-cylinder, single- or two-stage versions (the SPC-4 datasheet lists 2.5-11 kW, consistent with SPC-1 being the 1-cylinder unit, but the cylinder count is not printed for the SPC-1 so it is left in not_found). HTS leaflet: in re-liquefier mode the boil-off of the customer's LN2 (or LNe) bath flows to the cryogenerator and is condensed; LN2 sub-cooling to 68 K for cables uses external pumps and a pressurising vessel. Animation: crankshaft/pistons at 1455 rpm (24.25 Hz) in the ambient-temperature crankcase, helium shuttling to the cold head, N2 vapour entering and liquid dripping from the cold-head heat exchanger, water loop at 1200 l/h.
